purpose: Unify the four global template inequalities under one finite phase-cell extremum theorem.
core_observation: All four inequalities ask for extrema of sums of B_h=K_h W_h and E2=sum B_h^2 over finite offset/divisor templates with a<=400,h<=400.

proposed_master_theorem.name: finite_phase_cell_extremum
proposed_master_theorem.statement: For fixed cutoff A=400 and fixed layer rules, any extremum of a linear/quadratic functional in B_h over x in a scale window occurs on a finite list of phase cells determined by changes of floors floor(x/a), floor(2x/a), and divisibility templates a|x+h; within each cell the functional is monotone/convex enough to be checked at endpoints or stationary points from an explicit derivative table.

maps.functional: maximize U80 and V80 subject to U80>=0.16
derive Qmax(S), A(S), B(Q) by S/Q bins

proof_components_needed: phase cell decomposition for divisibility templates a|x+h with a<=400
within-cell formula for B_h using fixed floors and delta terms
derivative/stationary point bound for each term and each functional
monotonicity or convex envelope for bin/frontier constraints
risk: This is still a significant proof obligation; current repo has finite-window certificates but not the general phase-cell theorem.
